output.methodChoice: A+D: competing-hypotheses weighing plus careful reasoning, because the question is whether a single week lies within normal variation and which rival explains the rollout gap.
output.brief: The rise from 0.31% to 0.41% is most likely ordinary week-to-week variation. Over the previous 26 weeks the rate averaged 0.354% and the normal band's upper edge is 0.482%. 0.41% sits inside that band. Three earlier weeks were higher (0.44%, 0.47% and 0.51%) and were investigated with no fault found. The burn-rate page did not fire (0.82x against a 2x threshold). The dashboard count matches raw logs, so this is not a counting artefact. Dario's finding that new pods error more is real, but it is a warm-up effect. New pods start with an empty cache and time out on the database. The same gap appeared in all five recent rollouts, including a config-only redeploy, so it does not show a v4.18 fault. It adds only 10–20 errors per rollout, against a weekly rise of about 2,300 errors. Booking completion did not change. I would not roll back, and I would not mute alerting. Muting the burn-rate page would remove the protection that catches real problems. Record the week as within the normal band and apply the standard check to the following week. If next week's rate exceeds 0.48% or the page fires, investigate then. I can't rule out the replica move or partner-sync's month-end run as small contributors. I'm fairly confident in this conclusion.
